rules_text:
Rules summary The goal of Bombay is to have the most rupees at the end of the game. Players will earn rupees from buying the different colored silk bales from the trading posts and selling them in the cities, collecting City Tokens, Client Tokens and building Palaces. Players start their turn with 3 action tokens. Each type of action may be performed more than once (exception: buying silk bales). The possible actions and their costs are: Move to an adjacent intersection for 1 or 2 action tokens, depending on the intersection. Buy a silk bale for 1 or 2 action tokens and 1 or 2 rupees, depending on the color / trading post. *You may only buy one silk bale each turn* Sell a silk bale in a city for 1 action token. Build a Palace for 1 action token and 1 silk bale. Players may also " consolidate their fortune " and get 1 rupee from the bank instead of performing actions. Selling : you receive rupees according to the demand of each city and the good sold moves to the bottom: Top - 4 rupees Middle - 3 rupees Bottom - 1 rupee and 1 Client Token. Bonus: yellow silk bales sell for 1 extra rupee and purple silk bales sell for 1 extra client token. Palaces : you may spend any one silk bale to build a palace of your color in any intersection without a palace built and receive any bonus tokens at that location. Whenever an opponent goes to a spot with one of your palaces, you receive 1 rupee from the bank. Bonus tokens : Client Token Bonus, City Token Bonus, 2 Rupees Bonus, Silk Bale Bonus (choose a silk bale from the leftmost market to get for free). At the end of the game, players receive rupees according to majority of Palaces + Client Tokens : 2 player game: 1st = 4, 2nd = 0 3 player game: 1st = 6, 2nd = 2, 3rd 0 4 player game: 1st = 8, 2nd = 4, 3rd 2, 4th = 0 5 player game: 1st = 8, 2nd = 6, 3rd 4, 4th = 2, 5th = 0 City Tokens : you receive one City Token of the color corresponding to that city when you sell a silk bale there for the first time, provided there are still tokens of that color left. Bonus City Tokens can also be gained by building a Palace in an intersection with such a token. You may only have one City Token of each color. At the end of the game, players receive: 0 rupees for 1 or 2 different City Tokens 4 rupees for 3 different City Tokens 8 rupees for 4 different City Tokens The player with the most rupees wins. Ties are broken by the number of Client Tokens.

community_text:
[Rating: 2/10] Beautiful bits.Very light, with a nice theme that makes sense. But the games ends way too fast.  As it is I do not like it.  Maybe I should try to houserule the number of turns?

[Rating: 2/10] skip your turns and you'll be just as competitive as your opponents.  ship a single good and skip the rest of the turns and you might just win.  waste of 30 minutes of my life.

[Rating: 2/10] Szerintem túlértékelt játék. Szépnek még talán szép, de semmi eredeti nincs benne. Unalmas.

[Rating: 2/10] What a disappointment.  Absolutely no tension to this game.  Great components, artwork wasted on dull play.  Makes no sense that you can't have more than 1 elephant in a city (what?!!)  Has spatial play that I like in games, wanted to like this.

[Rating: 2/10] I really didn't want to believe all the bad reviews and took a risk with a cheap copy on Tanga. Unfortunately, I was disappointed. The rulebook was terrible, and did not make clear how to alter the game for three players. I still don't really know if we played right.   Regardless, you have so few things to do on your turn that the game really does get boring after just a couple of turns. Pick up a cube, go deliver a cube, maybe build a palace. Really a boring game.

[Rating: 2.5/10] Initial impression:  This game has no reason to exist/be purchased/played, even by players looking for a lighter pick-up/deliver game.  I'm very disappointed in Ystari with this release.  They've been somewhat hit-and-miss in the pass, as is to be expected, but this is a terrible miss.

[Rating: 3/10] This one really got on my nerves - what a waste of some pretty elephant pieces! The choices are all predicated on the cubes that are available and the game just seems too simplistic for its own good. I am aware that others will find this a much better game than me, but it really struck a sour chord with me and I really disliked it on a level I can't even describe or really justify.

[Rating: 3/10] [b][url=http://www.boardgamegeek.com/thread/410012/video-review-bombay]Dice Tower Reviews: Bombay[/url][/b]

[Rating: 3/10] My wife loves India, and so, in the tradition of giving me gifts that she might like, I received Bombay. Despite the attractive box art, it sat in 'the dark place' for some time before we decided to give it some attention.  As a simulation this works well; it's a 'pick up and deliver' game which moves slower than gastropod post in a tropical storm.  The most fun we had was deciding what to do with the elephant models after we barbecued the game board.  Decorations for sub-continent themed cup cakes anyone?

[Rating: 3/10] My rating probably wouldn't be so low except the chemical smell of the plastic in the game made me feel sick.  Would take some real convincing to get me to play this again.

[Rating: 3/10] The components are fun (plastic elephants that can carry wooden cubes) and the game is nice and light. It does seem to be a little too restrictive, though. It can take three or four turns just to pick up a cube, move to a different part of the board, and make a delivery. I know that the game is meant to be that way, but I prefer when a game feels a little more open. Still, I'll see how this holds up after some more plays.   Sold.

[Rating: 3/10] I think a good logistical game needs a decent sense of speed, and the ability to make high risk, high reward routes. Bombay feels slow and steady. Like an elephant. Very forgettable.

[Rating: 3/10] Only played online once. Pick up and deliver. Honestly didn't quite pick up or read the rules but the gameplay or graphics didn't draw me in.
